reasoning: The baseline Random Forest (cv=0.697) suffers from high train/CV gap (0.17), indicating overfitting on the small dataset (n=1252, p=49). The previous voting ensemble (iter01_c1) improved CV to 0.726 with soft voting of LR and RF but still has a non-zero gap. Literature suggests feature selection is critical for small tabular biomedical data [ev_892146c13f0a85]. We propose three distinct directions: 1) A pipeline applying RFE to reduce dimensionality before a Gradient Boosting model, leveraging the RFE evidence [ev_67cadb757a26d2] and GB's ability to handle non-linearities. 2) Refining the previous successful voting ensemble by increasing regularization (lower C for LR) and adjusting RF depth to test robustness against overfitting. 3) A simple, low-complexity baseline using Logistic Regression with strong L2 regularization (low C) to establish a lower bound and compare against complex ensembles. The baseline Random Forest achieved a CV mean of 0.6972 with a high train/test gap (0.1743), indicating overfitting or insufficient regularization. The previous voting ensemble (iter01_c1) improved performance to 0.7256 by combining Logistic Regression and Random Forest, reducing the gap significantly. However, it used standard scaling which may not be optimal for all feature types in this specific dataset profile, and the ensemble size is small. To address the high train/test gap and leverage the evidence regarding feature selection (RFE) and ensemble diversity, I propose three distinct configurations: 1) A refined voting ensemble with a stronger Gradient Boosting model and adjusted hyperparameters to test if boosting complements RF better than LR in this context. 2) A pipeline approach incorporating Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) as suggested by the literature evidence, feeding into a HistGradientBoosting classifier which is often more robust on tabular data with high dimensionality. 3) An ensemble using Extreme Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression with different regularization strengths to test if varying C values improves generalization compared to the previous RF+LR combination.
